subject: general
question: The rocky outer part of Earth is called:
solution:
The correct answer is __**the lithosphere**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The rigid, rocky outer layer of the Earth is called the lithosphere, it consist of the crust and the solid outermost layer of the upper **mantle**.
 
• It depth of it is extended to **100km**.
 
• It comprises the rocks of the earth’s crust and the thin layers of soil that contain nutrient elements that **sustain organisms**.
 
• The earth’s surface has **2** main divisions.
 
• The large land masses are known as the **continents** and the huge water bodies are called the **ocean basins**.
 
• There are 2 types of the **lithosphere**, one is oceanic lithosphere and other one is continental lithosphere.
 
• The oceanic lithosphere is associated with the **oceanic crust**, and it is slightly denser than the continental lithosphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Earth's **outer** core is a fluid layer about 2,260 km thick, composed of mostly iron and nickel that lies above Earth's solid inner core and below its mantle.
 
• The **inner** core is the innermost layer of the Earth and is located at the direct center of the Earth below the outer core.
 
• The **mantle** lies between Earth's dense, super-heated core and its thin outer layer, the crust.
